rv.q: Instead, Steppenwolf Theatre Company is staging the world premiere of a predictable moral satire, which is of course not a satire at all...
As always at Steppenwolf, Walker is supported by some brilliant design work.
Walker’s play works best when the satirical barbs and hysterical one-liners move like a high-spirited pickleball match.
Satirizing the fears of conservative women desperate to shield their children from material that threatens their values, Adirondack Chair Circle too often seems to be shooting fish in a barrel.
In other words, one problem with “Adirondack Chair Circle” is that even the winning, and the losing, feels anti-climactic.
This is the kind of juicy uneasy theatre which Steppenwolf excels at.
The entire production is more validation that Steppenwolf seems to always know its audiences, even with accomplished satire that could very well have already happened here and there in America.
It’s very funny, somewhat thought-provoking, and perfectly executed in its world premiere under Pam MacKinnon’s direction at Steppenwolf Theatre Company.
Under the masterful direction of Pam MacKinnon, this show is tight, funny, and a little more than disturbing.
That combination adds up to an entertaining evening of theater. But for a satire, 'Adirondack Chair Circle' lacks bite.

This premiere by Chicago suburban native Stephanie Alison Walker about book-banning moms shows a surprising amount of compassion for people who espouse loathsome views, without making us agree with them.
Adirondack Chair Circle is an extremely funny play that's preaching to the choir.
For all its considerable virtues, that's the one thing Walker's play never quite delivers.
But Adirondack Chair Circle offers little to challenge the people already on its side, either.
Not even a solid cast and tragically relevant subject matter can save Adirondack Chair Circle from a scattered script that should still be in Drafts.
“Adirondack Chair Circle” is a snapshot of our time, and it is timeless in its appeal.

This is a well written, nicely performed, thought provoking play that might have you considering how much control parents are entitled to have when it comes to ideas that might be considered controversial to some and how much we are willing to sacrifice for our cause.
The cast is so spot-on that it almost carried the day, despite the extra unnecessary hour in length.

cn.t: Mixed reviews greet this Steppenwolf world premiere: critics praise its sharp wit and Katrina Lenk's performance, but many fault the script for preaching to the choir with a stacked deck rather than challenging its liberal audience.
